reference: No matching GNU wg CLI is assumed. Contracts use the loadable's Bash type/help interface, RFC 7748 X25519 test-vector bytes encoded with standard base64, the documented key-format/clamping rules, and an independently assembled Linux WireGuard generic-netlink message. In the dry-run case only the per-call sequence field is variable; the remaining message bytes and length are fixed by the independent encoder. Python standard base64 independently verifies all scalar clamp bits in a generated test value.
coverage: Bash loadable availability metadata and help text
wg genkey output length, standard base64 alphabet, padding and Curve25519 clamp bits
pubkey invalid-input status and show missing-interface usage status
setconf dry-run parsing and encoded generic-netlink attributes for a small Interface plus one IPv4/IPv6 peer
rejection of an IPv4 AllowedIPs prefix longer than 32 bits
exclusions: No matching GNU CLI is available as an independent command oracle, so no case is labeled GNU parity.
Actual set, show, and setconf netlink operations require a disposable WireGuard-enabled VM and are deferred. Dry-run checks stop before opening a netlink socket.
No live network traffic, interface creation, route changes, kernel changes, credentials, or host paths are used.

cases.purpose: Check the Bash builtin type contract and that help exposes the documented WireGuard summary, setconf verb, and dry-run note.
Check pubkey against RFC 7748 Alice's fixed X25519 scalar/public-key vector; the base64 strings are independently encoded from the RFC hex bytes.

Independently decode one generated key with Python standard base64 and check all three X25519 clamp bits, exact 32-byte length and canonical encoding. This uses no installed or operational credential; random contents and entropy quality are not asserted.
cases.script:
key=$(wg genkey)
/usr/bin/python3 - "$key" <<'PYKEY'
import base64,sys
key=sys.argv[1]
assert len(key)==44 and key.endswith('=')
raw=base64.b64decode(key,validate=True)
assert len(raw)==32 and base64.b64encode(raw).decode()==key
assert raw[0]&7==0 and raw[31]&128==0 and raw[31]&64==64
print('valid-clamped-key')
PYKEY

cases.purpose: Check that pubkey rejects input that is not a 32-byte standard-base64 key and emits no public-key bytes.
Check the documented slice-A usage contract that show requires one explicit interface; the missing-argument path returns before netlink access.

Exercise a bounded setconf parser fixture in BASHWG_DRY mode and compare every fixed netlink byte against an independent Linux UAPI encoder. The time/PID-derived 32-bit nlmsg sequence at byte offsets 8..11 is the sole omitted field; output length, framing, header prefix, and all other bytes are checked.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' '[Interface]' 'PrivateKey = dwdtCnMYpX08FsFyUbJmRd9ML4frwJkqsXf7pR25LCo=' 'ListenPort = 51820' 'FwMark = 0x1234' '[Peer]' 'PublicKey = hSDwCYkwp1R0i33ctD73Wg2/Og0mOBr066SpjqqbTmo=' 'Endpoint = 192.0.2.1:51820' 'AllowedIPs = 10.0.0.0/24, 2001:db8::/32' 'PersistentKeepalive = 25' > wg.conf
out=$(BASHWG_DRY=1 wg setconf wg0 wg.conf)
summary=${out%%$'\n'*}
[[ $summary == 'BASHWG_DRY: WG_CMD_SET_DEVICE (setconf) iface=wg0 peers=1 msg-len=240' ]] || exit 1
wire=${out#*$'\n'}
[[ $wire != "$out" ]] || exit 1
hex=${wire//$'\n'/}
hex=${hex// /}
[[ ${#hex} -eq 480 ]] || exit 1
case "$hex" in *[!0123456789abcdef]*) exit 1 ;; esac
[[ ${hex:0:16} == f000000000000500 ]] || exit 1
[[ ${hex:24} == '' ]] || exit 1
line_count=0
while IFS= read -r line; do
  ((line_count+=1))
  [[ ${#line} -eq 39 ]] || exit 1
done <<< "$wire"
[[ $line_count -eq 15 ]] || exit 1
printf 'independent-netlink-encoding-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Require standard IPv4 CIDR validation to reject /33. BASHWG_DRY prevents kernel access, so only config parsing is exercised; this assertion is independent of the candidate's current mask handling.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' '[Peer]' 'PublicKey = hSDwCYkwp1R0i33ctD73Wg2/Og0mOBr066SpjqqbTmo=' 'AllowedIPs = 192.0.2.0/33' > wg.conf
BASHWG_DRY=1 wg setconf wg0 wg.conf

cases.purpose: Validate actual device mutation and kernel acknowledgement for wg set.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable WireGuard-enabled Linux VM with an isolated test interface, generic-netlink family support, and CAP_NET_ADMIN. The harness intentionally has no capabilities and cannot safely apply kernel device state.

cases.purpose: Validate decoding and formatting of real device and peer state returned by the kernel for wg show IFACE.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable WireGuard-enabled Linux VM with a preconfigured test interface and peer state so the GET_DEVICE reply can be checked against the independent wg(8) contract. No live kernel query is attempted here.

cases.purpose: Validate that a valid configuration is applied to a WireGuard device and can be read back from kernel state.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable WireGuard-enabled Linux VM, an isolated test interface, and CAP_NET_ADMIN for setconf plus a read-back query. The local dry-run contract only validates parsing and encoded bytes, not application.

cases.purpose: The CLI and config file share CIDR validation: an ordinary IPv4 /33 is rejected with CLI usage status 2, under explicit dry-run mode before netlink access.
cases.script:
export BASHWG_DRY=1
wg set wg0 peer hSDwCYkwp1R0i33ctD73Wg2/Og0mOBr066SpjqqbTmo= allowed-ips 192.0.2.0/33

cases.purpose: Preserve valid family-specific CIDR boundaries and host defaults, including IPv6 /33. Check independent address-attribute and mask-attribute byte encodings while ignoring only unrelated message fields; all calls explicitly stop in dry-run mode.
